response.markdown_report:
The strongest next experiment remains **gradually introduced, bounded negative weighting within corrected BERT4Rec**, with narrower claims and explicit gradient controls. At 30% progress, its local implementation is preferable to immediately adding text or temporal attention.

Three starting insights guide the proposal. First, Electronics has 11.89% negative-over-positive training conflicts and a negative tenth-percentile margin: inspected training discrimination is imperfect, but held-out failure is unproven. Second, users distinguish broad relevance from specific usefulness; harder competition could help, but cannot establish ownership, compatibility or current need. Third, diagnostic coverage exists in every category; deployment parity and consumed-record provenance remain unavailable.

Three literature insights refine the intervention. RotatE establishes precedent for detached negative weighting, reducing novelty. Hard-BPR actually suppresses extreme-negative gradients; bounded increasing weights do not. Contrastive-loss analyses distinguish negative allocation from aggregate pressure: candidate CE already emphasizes high scores, so additional weighting may duplicate that emphasis.

| Direction | Atomic proposal | Evidence and gap |
|---|---|---|
| Optimization | Bounded weighting of existing K=16 negatives | Small change; preserves extreme-score domination |
| Semantic specificity | Joint scratch-trained title guidance in attention | NOVA-BERT; requires target-text masking |
| Temporal relevance | Near-zero-initialized time-gap attention bias | TiSASRec; omitted sensitivity outcomes establish no preferred recency direction |

Scores use O/P/U/M/D for originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bounded weighting | 2/6/5/7/5 | O: controlled adaptation; P: interpretable; U: contextual competition; M: observed conflicts; D: local loss | O: strong precedent; P: redundant emphasis; U: indirect; M: training exposure; D: controls and integration |
| Title attention guidance | 5/8/8/6/7 | O: constrained adaptation; P: extensible; U: specific cues; M: richer distinctions; D: one network | O: prior art; P: sparse supervision; U: missing specifications; M: no measured text deficit; D: writer changes |
| Time-gap bias | 4/7/8/5/6 | O: BERT adaptation; P: temporal learning; U: current intent; M: contextual separation; D: few parameters | O: established mechanism; P: sparse timestamps; U: recency assumptions; M: omitted sensitivity; D: timestamp routing |

Select bounded weighting as a feasible test of **loosely related items displacing specific matches** and **unsupported specialized equipment receiving high ranks**. Both links remain indirect hypotheses; extreme negatives are not demonstrably moderated. Electronics’ measured ranking conflicts provide the model-facing target.

Warm up uniformly, then introduce detached normalized weights. For S=Σwⱼexp(nⱼ−p), the loss is log(1+S), negative allocation is qⱼ=wⱼexp(nⱼ−p)/S, and aggregate mass is M=S/(1+S). Normalization fixes neither mass nor parameter-gradient norms. Compare uniform and full weighting first; budget permitting, separate allocation, pressure and timing effects.

Preserve one model per category and appended-mask inference. Select solely by pinned sampled-candidate macro validation HR@10. Report category differences, helped/harmed users and paired uncertainty when available; disclose adaptive search and freeze selection before held-out evaluation. Sampled gains do not establish full-catalog improvement.

idea.description: Test a warm-start curriculum of bounded, detached hardness weights on the same 16 uniformly sampled negatives in the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Keep one independently trained network/checkpoint per category. Change only the masked-target candidate-ranking loss; preserve architecture, corruption, terminal-mask allocation, sampling eligibility and inference. Describe the intervention as a joint change in negative-gradient allocation, aggregate gradient pressure and timing, rather than moderate-negative selection or false-negative suppression.
idea.motivation: Electronics has 181 negative-over-positive conflicts among 1,522 inspected training targets (11.89%) and a tenth-percentile margin of -0.2245. This supports investigating contextual discrimination, without establishing false negatives or held-out failure. The user-facing hypotheses are that stronger contextual competition could reduce loosely related recommendations displacing specific matches and unsupported specialized equipment receiving high ranks. These links are indirect: candidate CE already emphasizes high-scoring negatives, and additional weighting may amplify uncertain competitors without improving usefulness. Interaction supervision cannot certify compatibility, ownership, redundancy, quantities or immediate need. Current diagnostics inspected ten batches per category; instrumentation must preserve this measured coverage rather than claim to restore missing coverage. At 30% progress, retain the small intervention but lower originality and potential ratings, increase integration difficulty, and reserve text and temporal architecture changes for separate experiments.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is integration code for the supplied baseline, whose source is absent from the prompt, not an executable replacement train.py. Audit the actual baseline objective, negative count, eligibility, replacement, target/example reduction, optimizer, clipping, stopping and checkpoint policy before applying it. The proposed control is uniform candidate CE/K=16. If the supplied baseline differs, retain it as the benchmark anchor and disclose objective/count changes; do not call an anchor comparison weighting-only. No shell inspection or training is performed in this response.

Weight definition: for each valid masked target, let d_j = negative_logit_j - positive_logit. Define detached h_j = sigmoid(d_j), r_j = 1 + alpha*h_j, and w_j = 16*r_j/sum(r). For alpha in [0,1], weights have mean one and lie within [1/(1+alpha), 1+alpha], hence [0.5,2]. Optimize L_w = log(1 + sum_j w_j*exp(d_j)) with stable FP32 arithmetic. No logQ correction or full-softmax equivalence is claimed. Detachment defines a semi-gradient update and does not differentiate the complete score-dependent weighting function. RotatE supplies clear precedent for detached score-based weights, although it weights separate logistic losses rather than this candidate-CE denominator.

Correct interpretation: ordinary candidate CE already assigns exponential emphasis to high-scoring negatives. Saturating additional weights bounds extra amplification but leaves exponential domination intact. This rule neither prefers moderate negatives nor suppresses extreme-negative gradients. Hard-BPR's declining gradient at extreme negative margins is a distinct mechanism and a possible future loss experiment, not a property of this proposal. A pool of only 16 uniform negatives also limits the challenging candidates available. Negative-over-positive conflicts are not measured false negatives.

Gradient decomposition: set S_w=sum_j w_j*exp(d_j), q_wj=w_j*exp(d_j)/S_w and M_w=S_w/(1+S_w). With detached weights, dL_w/dn_j=M_w*q_wj and dL_w/dp=-M_w; total absolute logit-gradient mass is 2*M_w. Parameter gradients equal M_w*sum_j q_wj*(grad n_j-grad p). Therefore equal weight sums fix neither allocation, aggregate mass, parameter-gradient norms, nor optimizer updates. Jacobian alignment, cancellation, clipping and Adam state all matter.

Schedule: use E=min(int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS','200')),200), requiring E>=1, and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Warm up for ceil(0.2*E) epochs, then increase alpha linearly to one over the remaining declared epochs. If none remain, retain uniform weights. Tie the schedule to declared epochs, not the selected checkpoint, and record completed epochs, selected epoch, active steps and realized strength exposure. These numerical choices are proposed settings rather than validated optima.

Candidates and randomness: keep exactly the same K=16 uniform candidate draws, replacement policy, exclusions and across-target reduction as the audited uniform control. Retain repeated-ID multiplicities and report unique-item counts. Use training information only for eligibility; PAD, MASK and the target cannot be negatives. Preserve any additional baseline training-history exclusions without silently adding new ones. Count empty eligible sets and empty supervised batches; use the baseline's documented handling without NaN reductions. Preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Use explicit purpose-separated RNG streams for users/crops, corruption, negatives and diagnostics, derived from stable integer keys and a fixed category order. Keep condition identifiers out of matched streams. Verify matching users, crops, labels, masks and candidate multisets with recorded hashes. Introducing RNG isolation changes a shared-stream baseline, so distinguish matched controls from the unchanged host anchor. A common seed does not imply matched inputs or cross-platform determinism.

Comparison priority: first compare uniform CE/K=16 against scheduled full weighting over all four categories. Comparison models start independently from seed 42, never from another trial's checkpoint, and are never combined. If sufficient shared budget remains for complete four-category configurations, add allocation-only and pressure-only controls. At each variant's own current parameters and identical candidate logits, compute baseline mass M_0 and weighted mass M_w. Allocation-only uses stopgrad(M_0/M_w)*L_w; pressure-only uses stopgrad(M_w/M_0)*L_0. Apply scaling per target before the unchanged reduction. These identities hold locally at identical parameters and candidates; independently trained variants diverge and do not maintain matched masses along their trajectories. Compute ratios through stable log masses, check finiteness and disclose any numerical failure rather than silently clipping ratios. The bounded weights bound the mass ratios, but do not bound all model gradients.

Timing controls: the earlier optional immediate-weighting-throughout control changes both timing and cumulative exposure, so it cannot isolate curriculum order. If timing is investigated, predeclare early, delayed and reproducibly shuffled intervention windows with identical active-step counts, the same multiset of strengths, total updates, learning-rate schedule and sampled inputs. Keep the original warm-up/ramp as the primary practical policy. Report cumulative prescribed strength separately from realized allocation change, excess mass and update norms, which depend on the fitted trajectory. Checkpoint selection may truncate delivered exposure and must be reported. Do not launch every optional control automatically.

Measurements: on bounded, predeclared steps, record weights, baseline/weighted allocation entropy and top-1/top-4 negative-gradient shares, M_0/M_w distributions, conflict rates, sparse positive/negative logit-gradient summaries, clipping frequency and actual optimizer-update norms. Where affordable, use explicit autograd measurements of per-example and batch parameter-gradient norms and cosine similarity, distinguishing pre-clipping, post-clipping and optimizer updates. Logit gradients cannot substitute for these measurements. A separate batch-gradient-norm-matched comparison is optional and requires an explicit gradient-rescaling implementation; matching logit mass alone does not implement it. Diagnostic measurement must not change optimization or consume training RNG. Record unavailable measurements as unavailable.

Budget and execution: all training, optional gradient measurements, diagnostics, debugging and failures count against 43,200 summed GPU-seconds. Prioritize complete four-category primary comparisons before optional mechanistic controls and use actual runtime estimates before launching them. Four concurrent slots do not reduce aggregate GPU consumption. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, supplied splits, single-GPU execution and all routes in fixed order: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep maximum epochs 200 and batches per epoch 200. Never read other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

Inference and deployment: retain the corrected BERT4Rec architecture and existing embedded predictor writer, matching the selected checkpoint's architecture/configuration, item mappings and reserved IDs. Each category loads exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint. Construct left_pad(history[-(L-1):]+[MASK], L), require sufficient sequence capacity, and read the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Hide each supervised target at its selected position from bidirectional inputs; legitimate earlier repeats may remain. Exclude PAD and MASK as recommendation candidates. If a fresh-process runner is supported, compare the generated predictor against the strictly reloaded selected checkpoint on identical short, truncated and supported empty histories and real candidate IDs. Preserve the supplied audit tolerances and record fixtures, errors and rank disagreements. Live-model agreement does not establish exported-checkpoint parity; unavailable runners remain unavailable.

Diagnostic contract: retain family-specific sample_batch and ModelView, view.model as the actual nn.Module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), constructing its interpretation prompt from measured metrics and definitions. Loader tuples remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors; K-negative tensors stay internal to training. Preserve the existing fixed-one-negative diagnostic protocol, including actual inspected batch and valid-target counts. Use an independent disposable diagnostic loader/RNG and restore model mode afterward. Preserve existing measured coverage; do not confuse unavailable consumed-record provenance with missing masked-target coverage. Capture bounded actual production records only through a supported side channel. Unavailable provenance, attention hooks and exported-predictor runners remain unavailable rather than becoming claimed passes. Angular embedding alignment alone does not establish harmful collapse, and omitted history-sensitivity outcomes establish no recency conclusion.

Evaluation and uncertainty: select only through pinned host sampled-candidate macro validation HR@10, using 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Report actual hits/200, each category's HR@10 and paired absolute delta, plus the equally weighted macro delta. One changed hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. If paired outcomes are supplied, report helped/harmed discordant counts and 10,000 seed-42 paired bootstrap resamples of users within each category, recomputing macro differences and a percentile 95% interval. Otherwise mark paired uncertainty unavailable. These intervals condition on fitted models, fixed candidates and the four datasets; they exclude training/candidate-resampling variability, new-dataset generalization and adaptive selection bias. Disclose every inspected configuration/checkpoint, failures, costs and selection/tie rules. Treat validation gains as exploratory after adaptive search, freeze the final choice before independent held-out evaluation, and never inspect hidden test information. Fixed seeds and unique candidates do not remove sampled-metric bias or establish full-catalog gains. The twenty-user full-catalog simulator exercise remains limited qualitative feedback, not the selection metric.

Risks and scope: weighting may emphasize frequent items, high-norm scores, repeated training targets or uncertain negatives, and may merely amplify CE's existing preference rather than improve contextual specificity. Preserve baseline regularization and stopping; avoid post-hoc tuning of alpha, schedule or weight shape without recording another inspected configuration. Track available training-frequency and history-length strata descriptively, without inventing compatibility or relevance labels. A null or negative result should motivate reassessment rather than unreported tuning. No independent popularity/transition scores, ensembles, checkpoint averaging, separately fitted experts, pretrained weights or extra datasets enter the experiment. Only public histories, item titles/descriptions and timestamps are available; ratings, review text, structured categories/prices/stores and simulator diversity/conformity traits must remain unused. If a later text-guided architecture is tested, mask all target-position text features and update the predictor writer within that separate single-network experiment.
idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def weighting_strength(epoch, maximum_epochs):
    E = min(int(maximum_epochs), 200)
    if E < 1 or not 0 <= epoch < E:
        raise ValueError('Invalid epoch schedule')
    warm = math.ceil(0.2 * E)
    if epoch < warm or warm == E:
        return 0.0
    return (epoch - warm + 1) / (E - warm)


def bounded_masked_candidate_loss(
    positive_logits, negative_logits, alpha, mode='full'
):
    """Per-target losses and detached weights; aggregate externally.

    mode='uniform': ordinary candidate CE.
    mode='full': bounded weighted candidate CE.
    mode='allocation_only': weighted allocation, local baseline logit mass.
    mode='pressure_only': baseline allocation, local weighted logit mass.
    Each optional mode is a separate experiment, never inference fusion.
    """
    if not math.isfinite(float(alpha)) or not 0.0 <= alpha <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError('alpha must be finite and in [0, 1]')
    if mode not in {'uniform', 'full', 'allocation_only', 'pressure_only'}:
        raise ValueError('Unknown loss mode')
    p = positive_logits.reshape(-1).float()
    n = negative_logits.float()
    if n.shape != (p.numel(), 16):
        raise ValueError('Expected exactly 16 negatives per target')
    if p.numel() == 0:
        raise ValueError('Caller must skip/count empty supervised batches')
    if not torch.isfinite(p).all() or not torch.isfinite(n).all():
        raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite logits')

    d = n - p[:, None]
    with torch.no_grad():
        raw = 1.0 + alpha * torch.sigmoid(d.detach())
        weights = raw / raw.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)

    # L = softplus(log S), avoiding explicit exponentiation of large scores.
    log_s0 = torch.logsumexp(d, dim=-1)
    log_sw = torch.logsumexp(d + weights.log(), dim=-1)
    loss0 = F.softplus(log_s0)
    lossw = F.softplus(log_sw)

    # log M = log sigmoid(log S); all scaling factors are detached.
    with torch.no_grad():
        log_m0 = F.logsigmoid(log_s0.detach())
        log_mw = F.logsigmoid(log_sw.detach())
        allocation_scale = torch.exp(log_m0 - log_mw)
        pressure_scale = torch.exp(log_mw - log_m0)

    if mode == 'uniform':
        losses = loss0
    elif mode == 'full':
        losses = lossw
    elif mode == 'allocation_only':
        losses = allocation_scale * lossw
    else:
        losses = pressure_scale * loss0

    if not torch.isfinite(losses).all():
        raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite candidate loss')
    return losses, weights.detach()


# Integration specification: omitted APIs come from the corrected host baseline.
# Audit its objective, eligibility, replacement, reductions and selection policy.
# Retain the unchanged host anchor; distinguish any matched RNG-isolated control.
# DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts remain trial-local.
# E = min(int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')), 200); require E >= 1.
# Preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42.
#
# Primary experiments, only if enough budget remains for all four categories:
#   uniform CE/K=16 and scheduled full weighting CE/K=16.
# Optional allocation/pressure/timing experiments are separate trained models.
# Never average, fuse or reuse their checkpoints as initializations.
#
# For each declared experiment:
#   For each category in the fixed supplied order:
#     Initialize exactly one corrected BERT4Rec with seed 42.
#     Initialize purpose-separated matched RNG streams.
#     For epoch in range(E):
#       For step in range(200):
#         Get unchanged baseline masked inputs, labels and target-row mapping.
#         Draw the same K=16 eligible uniform negatives as the matched control.
#         Preserve replacement, exclusions and repeated-ID multiplicities.
#         valid = (sequence == MASK) & (positive != PAD)
#         Skip/count empty eligible or empty supervised cases as documented.
#         features = model.log2feats(sequence)[valid]
#         p = model.predict_score(features, positive[valid])
#         n = model.predict_score(features, negative_ids_K16)
#         target_losses, weights = bounded_masked_candidate_loss(
#             p, n, weighting_strength(epoch, E), mode=declared_mode)
#         loss = audited_baseline_target_reduction(target_losses, target_rows)
#         Apply unchanged optimizer, learning-rate schedule and clipping.
#         On predeclared bounded steps, measure allocation, logit masses,
#         actual parameter gradients/clipping/update norms where supported.
#         Keep measurement RNG and forwards separate from production RNG.
#       Apply unchanged host-compatible validation/checkpoint policy.
#     Save exactly one selected checkpoint with its configuration and mappings.
#     Emit matching predictor code for that same architecture.
#
# Verify hashes of users/crops/labels/masks/candidate multisets across controls.
# Verify alpha=0 gives ordinary candidate CE and identical local gradients.
# At a fixed parameter state, verify optional control gradients satisfy:
#   allocation-only: dn_j = M0*q_wj, dp = -M0
#   pressure-only:   dn_j = Mw*q_0j, dp = -Mw
# These local identities do not imply matched independently trained trajectories.
#
# Optional timing controls must preserve the multiset of intervention strengths,

# Record prescribed exposure separately from realized trajectory-dependent effects.

#   score real candidates through the same model.predict_score
# Verify fresh-process parity only through a supported actual export runner.

# Log all inspected checkpoints/configurations and summed GPU-seconds.
# Freeze selection before independent held-out evaluation; no full-catalog claims.

originality.positive: The bounded rule and explicit allocation/pressure controls provide a clear, auditable adaptation to masked BERT4Rec with unchanged candidates and one scoring network.
originality.negative: RotatE establishes detached score-based weighting precedent, and candidate CE already emphasizes high scores. Normalization, warm starts and mechanistic controls offer limited algorithmic novelty.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could determine whether relative allocation, aggregate pressure or timing warrants further work before more expensive semantic or temporal changes.
future_potential.negative: Additional hardness emphasis may duplicate CE, amplify uncertain negatives and address user complaints only indirectly. Sampled-validation gains need not improve full-catalog usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary loss is short and preserves the BERT4Rec architecture, checkpoint format and inference path.
code_difficulty.negative: The earlier score of 3 understated baseline auditing, matched randomness, stable mechanistic controls, actual gradient measurements, budget management and trustworthy deployment diagnostics. The supplied baseline source remains necessary for executable integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the bidirectional masked-item backbone and Cloze training foundation preserved by this proposal.
Supports hiding supervised target information and using an appended reserved mask for next-item inference.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed bounded negative-weighting curriculum or its benchmark performance.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Modifies the pairwise loss so that, with a positive robustness parameter, gradient magnitude declines at both margin extremes.
Motivates examining uncertain hard negatives and distinguishes actual extreme-negative suppression from saturated increasing weights.
limitations: Its collaborative-filtering results do not establish gains for masked BERT4Rec candidate cross-entropy.
Does not identify which benchmark negatives are false negatives.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-start and controlled introduction of harder training competition.
limitations: The proposed weighting schedule is an adaptation rather than a reproduction of its sampling algorithm.
Its findings do not establish BERT4Rec effectiveness or isolate timing from cumulative intervention exposure here.

related_work.title: NOVA-BERT
contributions: Motivates separating attention-guiding side information from item-ID value representations.
Provides context for a future jointly trained title-guidance alternative.
limitations: Does not validate a scratch-trained title encoder under the supplied data and budget constraints.
A text adaptation requires hiding every associated feature at supervised target positions and updating exported inference consistently.

related_work.title: TiSASRec
contributions: Provides a mechanism for incorporating pairwise time intervals into sequential attention.
limitations: Uses a different original backbone and does not establish a beneficial recency direction for this task.
An adaptation must use observed history timestamps rather than an unavailable next-event timestamp.

related_work.title: RotatE official implementation: self-adversarial negative sampling
contributions: Demonstrates normalized score-dependent negative weights detached during backpropagation.
Establishes direct precedent that lowers the novelty of detached hardness weighting.
limitations: Weights negative logistic losses in knowledge-graph embedding rather than masked BERT4Rec candidate cross-entropy.
Normalization and detachment do not prevent concentration on uncertain high-scoring negatives.

related_work.title: Understanding the Behaviour of Contrastive Loss
contributions: Provides context for analyzing how contrastive objectives distribute penalties among negatives.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed weighting rule's recommendation performance.
The report's allocation/mass formulas follow directly from the specified loss and are not presented as this paper's exact algorithm.

related_work.title: Decoupled Contrastive Learning
contributions: Motivates distinguishing coupled gradient scaling from relative negative allocation.
limitations: Its objective and application differ from this masked recommendation experiment.
Matching logit-gradient mass does not guarantee matching parameter-gradient norms or optimizer updates.

related_work.title: When Do Curricula Work?
contributions: Motivates examining order effects with appropriate random-order curriculum controls.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed negative-weight schedule for BERT4Rec.
Order comparisons require matched prescribed exposure and still produce different training trajectories.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog rankings, including model orderings.
limitations: Does not invalidate controlled comparisons under the required pinned sampled-candidate benchmark.
Does not justify changing the host evaluator or claiming full-catalog gains from sampled HR@10.

related_work.title: Paired retrieval-evaluation methods
contributions: Provides methodological context for paired comparisons using the same evaluated users or queries.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified paired bootstrap requires actual paired user-level outcomes.
Conditional user-resampling intervals exclude training variability, candidate-resampling variability and adaptive-selection bias.

related_work.title: The Reusable Holdout: Preserving Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: Explains why repeated adaptive reuse of validation data can produce optimistic selected results.
limitations: Ordinary post-selection paired intervals do not correct this bias.
This experiment does not implement a reusable-holdout mechanism; it discloses search and freezes selection before host-held-out evaluation.
